title: The seed is a starting number
plain: A world is grown from one starting number, like a recipe card that every copy of the game reads the same way.

title: Each chunk has its own dice
plain: Every chunk rolls its dice from the world number plus its own address, so a player has no way to change the dice.

title: Biomes come from layers
plain: Deserts and forests are decided by stacking zoomed maps on top of each other, and the result depends only on the seed and where you look.

title: Hills come from smooth noise
plain: The ground height is a smooth wobbly surface computed from the seed, the same for everyone.

title: Chunks are built in steps
plain: A chunk is built like a cake in layers: shape, caves, then trees and ores last.

title: Seed crackers
plain: People can work out a world's number just by looking at a few trees and structures, which shows the world is a function of its number.

title: Trees and ores cross borders
plain: A tree or an ore blob near the edge of a chunk can stick out into the next chunk, so two chunks share some blocks.

title: Order bug reports
plain: Players reported that the same seed gave slightly different edges depending on which chunk the game built first.

title: Nobody says order never matters
plain: We searched for any source saying the build order can never matter, and found none.

title: Our server reads real chunks
plain: Our own copy of the game builds seed 7 in about 20 seconds and our reader decodes 7,360 real chunk slices from it.

title: Block transmutation is old
plain: Turning one block into another by tricking its hidden number worked in old versions and stopped for good in 2017.

title: Speedrun luck rolls
plain: Trading with piglins for pearls is a dice roll that changed between 1.16.1 and 1.16.2.

title: A misprinted percentage
plain: One famous report says 42 percent but its own counts, 42 of 262, give 16 percent, so the number cannot be trusted.
